subject: Proposal: Provisioning scale, burst pocket and new rate map
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@skylinemedia.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Provisioning scale, burst pocket and new rate map

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our conversation I’ve sketched out a proposed path to support Skyline’s expected Q3 product launch traffic without compromising latency for end users. High-level changes:

- Monthly committed throughput: increase from 5M tokens/month to 12M tokens/month (blended).
- Burst pocket: 20% monthly burst allowance for short spikes, with a per-spike throttle threshold of 600 rps for the hosted API route.
- New rate map: reduced per-token price at three tiers (base / mid / high) tied to monthly consumption bands — attached spreadsheet includes the math and projected cost delta.
- SLA addendum: 99.9% regional availability + faster escalation channel for production incidents.

I attached a provisioning schedule (Skyline_provisioning_schedule.xlsx) and a draft SLA addendum (SLA_addendum.pdf). Procurement asked for a single-year term with quarterly usage True-ups; pricing in the spreadsheet assumes an annual term with a 10% prepayment credit.

Can you confirm if the burst pocket and the uplifted monthly commit align with Skyline’s procurement constraints? If yes, I’ll circulate a redline for legal and send a DocuSign link for signatures.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm budget approach (prepay vs. quarterly).
2) We lock the start date and provisioning ramp in the attached schedule.
3) Legal redline -> DocuSign, then ops run provisioning.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

---
Attachments: Skyline_provisioning_schedule.xlsx, SLA_addendum.pdf

From: Elena Torres <elena@skylinemedia.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 11:19:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Provisioning scale, burst pocket and new rate map

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear plan. A few quick questions from procurement before we get legal involved: 

1) Burst pocket mechanics — is the 20% a rolling allowance or reset monthly? How do you measure a "spike" for billing purposes?
2) If we exceed the burst pocket twice in a month (two short spikes), how are overages billed? Is there a grace band?
3) The 10% prepay credit looks good for finance, but our procurement team prefers quarterly billing. Will the pricing table support quarterly invoices with the same unit rates (no prepay)?

We’d prefer to keep the annual start date as May 1, but procurement wants a 30-day negotiation window. Can you provide a version of the spreadsheet with a quarterly billing column and an explicit overage calculation?

Happy to take a 30-minute call Wednesday morning if that helps.

Best,
Elena
Head of Product Ops | Skyline Media
elena@skylinemedia.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Proposal: Provisioning scale, burst pocket and new rate map

Kim / Marissa —

Forwarding Elena's procurement questions (below). Need a quick internal alignment so we can respond with a doc that procurement can sign off on. Specific asks: 

- Can ops confirm whether the burst pocket is a calendar-month reset or a rolling window? Also need the exact counting rules (token measurement window, rounding) so I can include them in the contract language.
- Legal: if we allow quarterly billing at the same unit rates (no prepay credit), are there any billing mechanics or risk/credit points we should add (e.g., invoice cadence, late-payment grace)?
- Commercial: recommend we offer a one-time "first-quarter buffer" — allow 10% extra burst forgiveness in Q1 of the term to ease the transition. If ops agrees, we can bake that into the SOW.

Can one of you take ops/legal action items and I’ll prepare an updated spreadsheet (quarterly column + explicit overage formula) and a redline. Elena is available Wednesday morning for a 30-min call — suggest 9:30am PT.

Thanks,
Jordan

Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Provisioning scale, burst pocket and new rate map — updated materials and next steps

Elena / procurement —

Thanks for the pointed questions. We talked through the ops and legal items internally; below is the concise response and the attachments you requested.

Summary answers:
- Burst pocket mechanics: resets on a calendar month basis. Spikes are measured by sustained 1-minute token throughput exceeding the baseline average for the preceding 15-minute window. Billing counts tokens at the model output level; rounding is to the nearest 100 tokens.
- Overages: If you exhaust the 20% burst pocket, overage for the remainder of the month is billed at the "high" tier rate (explicit in the spreadsheet). We will provide two free overage forgiveness events per contract year (short spikes up to 10% each) as a goodwill buffer.
- Quarterly billing option: attached is a revised spreadsheet (quarterly column added) that preserves the same unit rates as the annual-prepay table; the 10% prepay credit is shown as an alternative for teams that want to prepay and lock price. Quarterly invoices will be net 30.

Attached: Skyline_provisioning_schedule.xlsx (updated), redline_contract_v2.docx (legal redline), and a link to the DocuSign envelope for signature: https://app.docusign.com/agree/ABCDEFG12345

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm quarterly billing or prepay by EOD Friday, Mar 20.
2) If procurement approves quarterly, we’ll remove the prepay credit line and send final DocuSign today. If prepay is selected, we’ll show final invoice schedule and apply the 10% credit on execution.
3) Ops will begin provisioning per the attached schedule with a May 1 start date (assuming signature by Apr 1).

Kimberly will follow up with a short call invite for Wednesday 9:30am PT if you want to go over the spreadsheet live.

Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
